> **Phase 110 (2026-11-22, branch `feat/stdlib-110-packaging` from `feat/stdlib-109-preconditions` @ `fd5b631`) — PACKAGING SPINE (decision D2a): the bundled standard library exists, the prelude merge is built, and the mechanism gate clause 2 will measure is live — carrying ONE entry end-to-end as its proof.** **The mechanism** (code commit `934214d`): library sources live in a new repo-root `stdlib/` directory (`stdlib/int.morph` this phase) and are embedded by `include_str!` — the codebase's standing embedding precedent — into a new `src/stdlib.rs`, which parses them once per process and serves two data surfaces: `prelude_specs()` (the entries' specs) and `shipped_body(name)` (each entry's crowned body as data — an IR construction in the Phase 92 denotation precedent). The merge lands at the two points every front door shares: `typeck::check` registers the library's signatures BEFORE the module's own, so a call to an entry typechecks with no import while the checked module itself stays exactly the user's (no prelude spec ever leaks into a module's spec list or a check report); and `SpecIndex::from_specs` / `from_module` insert the library's specs into the index, registering each shipped body alongside its spec. `SpecIndex::callee_body` consults the body registry FIRST — a shipped body is what its entry's name denotes — ahead of the row-derived denotations, which are untouched for every other name; `SpecIndex::empty()` and context-free judging carry no prelude, as before. CLI, API and playground/WASM all funnel through those two points (measured identical below), and **no bootstrap cascade appeared** — prelude entries are data, not builtins: the bootstrap-codegen suite stands at the same counts as default, the Codegen corpus and the synthesized artifact untouched. **The collision rule** (this phase's named deliverable, chosen as the conservative rule the brief prescribed): **a user module's own definition of a name WINS over the prelude entry of that name** — the prelude spec is not merged at all for a colliding name and its shipped body is not registered, so the user's spec denotes from its own rows with its own semantics; the rule is the typechecker's standing module-over-stdlib precedence applied to the merge itself, pinned at index level (spec + denotation) and at pipeline level (a module defining `int_abs` as the identity crowns its callers under identity semantics: `use_it(-3) = -3`, where the library gives 3). **The proof entry: `int_abs`** (`stdlib/int.morph`), carrying the frozen contract (STDLIB_SCOPE §2.2): two guarded rows in the established module dialect (negated-guard || consequent) plus the domain note as a `require:` — the Int minimum excluded, written out as `x != (0 - 9223372036854775807 - 1)` because the literal `-9223372036854775808` has no positive form the expression parser accepts (measured parse error). A measured contract-shape fact rides with it: the audit probe's disjunctive form (`output == x || output == (0 - x)`) crowns NOTHING through the pipeline (no seed family eats it — the seeded run crowned Inconclusive junk at 0/4 evaluable), while the guarded-row form crowns the faithful body; Phase 111's entries should be authored in seed-eatable shapes from the start. **The shipped body**, crowned at library-build time (seeded pipeline, seed 42) and transcribed into `src/stdlib.rs`: `if x < 0 { 0 - x } else { x }` — Z3-Verified against the entry's contract, 4/4 evaluable in-spec tests passed, the Int-minimum point spec-silent under the precondition (Phase 109's machinery, exercised end-to-end). The crowning is pinned, not just asserted: a suite test re-runs the pipeline over the library module and requires the crowned body to equal the shipped data exactly, so an engine change that moves the crown fails the suite until the library is re-crowned in the open. **End-to-end teeth** (`tests/phase110_prelude.rs`, 9 tests; the failing-first form was measured pre-change — the proof module failed typecheck with `Called undefined function: 'int_abs'`): a user module calling `int_abs` with no import line checks (its spec list unchanged), resolves (registry → `callee_body` → `inline_calls` substitutes the shipped body at the call site), and crowns a **Verified ∧ 3/3** caller through the CLI's stage sequence and through the API, with body identity between the two; the playground corpus gains the same module as a case (check + a synthesis pin measured from the native browser-profile harness — the crown is identical there, executed 3/3, status Inconclusive as that build honestly reports) and the corpus stands at **14/14 check + 6/6 synthesis** against the rebuilt bundle. **Invisibility when unused**, pinned: a standing module's check report lists exactly its own specs, its seeded crown is byte-identical to the pre-merge measurement (the validator winner: same body, 5/5/5), its own denotations are untouched, and the undefined-function diagnostic is unchanged. **`morphic init` corrected to reality**: the generated `Morphic.toml` no longer declares the fictional `morphic-std = "0.1"` dependency (the library ships with the compiler; there is nothing to depend on), and the generated `main.morph` no longer carries the fake `use morphic::std::*;` line — nor a bare top-level `spec`, nor unit-typed `main`: the old template did not even parse (measured parse error at the `use` line); the generated project is now a real module whose starter spec calls `int_abs`, and a test runs `init` + `check` through the actual binary. **Bundle**: rebuilt with the spine in place at **741,756 B ≤ 771,072 B budget** — +11,775 B over the standing 729,981 B, of which ~2.2 KB is the library source text itself and the rest one-time machinery (merge, registry, body data) that does not repeat per entry; **29,316 B of headroom remains for the ~29 entries of Phases 111–113, ≈ 1,010 B per entry** — inside the budget only with source economy in the library modules, or via gate clause 6's compressed / separately-loaded-asset route; the trajectory is named now so Phase 114's bundle clause is measured against it, not discovered at the gate. **Recorded boundaries for the entry phases**: the library declares no types this phase, so no prelude TYPE merge exists — `from_specs` keeps its documented no-types contract, and the first library type designs its merge when it exists; the interactive `morphic synthesize` path typechecks against the prelude, and its single-spec context-free synthesis resolves prelude calls exactly as it resolves sibling calls today (unchanged parity). **Suites: 591/0/30 default, 591/0/30 bootstrap-codegen, 461/0/22 no-Z3** — the Phase 109 baselines (582/582/453) + exactly the 9 new tests (8 in the no-Z3 configuration; the pipeline-crowning pin is Z3-gated). Code commit `934214d`; this note + the CHANGELOG entry are the docs commit. No scope or gate text changed — STDLIB_SCOPE.md stands frozen, and no fact correction was forced: the audit's merge point, the collision deliverable and the body-as-data design all landed as written. Next: Phase 111, the Int + Char core entries.

> **Phase 111 (2026-11-22, branch `feat/stdlib-111-int-char` from `feat/stdlib-110-packaging` @ `afbdfd8`) — INT + CHAR CORE ENTRIES: twelve of the frozen scope's fourteen §2.2/§2.3 entries ship (spec + pipeline-crowned body through the Phase 110 prelude); `int_gcd` does not ship — a named blocker, measured below; and the entries' cross-validation battery caught a standing executed-judge bug at the Int extremes, fixed minimally in this phase.** **The entries** (all Tier-1; every crown from the seeded pipeline, seed 42; every shipped body **Z3-Verified ∧ 100% golden-exact on its evaluable in-spec points**; the Phase 110 crowning pin is extended to re-run the pipeline over BOTH library modules and require every shipped body to equal its crown exactly — 13/13, `int_abs` included and unmoved): Int — `int_min` (complementary_guard → `If(a>b, b, a)`, 7/7), `int_max` (complementary_guard → `If(a<b, b, a)`, 7/7), `int_is_even` (equation → `x % 2 == 0`, 7/7), `int_is_odd` (equation → `x % 2 != 0`, 7/7), `int_clamp` (8/9 evaluable — the inverted-range point is spec-silent under `require: lo <= hi`), `int_sign` (7/7); Char — five classifiers as direct equations over the Char scalar encoding (`char_is_digit` 7/7, `char_is_alpha` 9/9, `char_is_whitespace` 6/6 — the tokenizer's set adopted exactly: space, tab, newline, carriage return — `char_is_uppercase` 6/6, `char_is_lowercase` 6/6) and `char_to_digit` (8/8). **Cross-validation** (gate clause 3's discipline, `tests/phase111_cross_validation.rs`): each entry executed against a hand-written Rust mirror over a battery far wider than its in-spec tests — **100% agreement on every pinned point** (Int: degenerate/typical/extremes incl. both endpoints and their neighbours — abs 16 pinned + 1 silent, sign 11, min/max 16 pairs each, clamp 13 + 2 silent, even/odd 15 each with the frozen complement property asserted; Char: a 101-point alphabet per entry — printable ASCII plus tab/newline/return, NUL, vertical tab (adversarial: NOT in the frozen whitespace set), DEL), spec-silent points reported in their own class, never as failures. **Contract-shape measurements** (Phase 110's finding, confirmed and extended): guard rows alone crown NOTHING for `int_clamp` or `int_sign`; each carries one further true row — the composition identity (`output == int_min(int_max(x, lo), hi)`, resp. `output == int_clamp(x, (0 - 1), 1)`) — which is the equation seed's shape and crowns the composed body, so **composition-equation crowning via sibling entries is now a proven library pattern** (sibling calls resolve through the prelude registry at judging time; a module-context verifier is required, pinned). Negative literals remain unparseable in constraint position and `(0 - 1)` fires no seed pin (no constant folding in `expr_to_ir`), which is why the composition row, not a three-region table, is sign's crowning shape. **The one seed-family addition: `char_guard_table`** (engine.rs, ~250 lines with helpers, priced as one small family). `char_to_digit`'s frozen form — guard rows pinning CONSTRUCTED values (`Some(d)` / `None()`) — was unseedable: the Int guard table's pin test demands `IRLiteral` pins and exists to refuse exactly these. The judge side was always ready (a hand-written Match body Verifies ∧ 7/7 against the corrected spec); the gap was seed-side only. The family restates the guard table's joint falsify-every-leaf recovery for a Char key over the scalar span widened ±2, generalizes pins to arbitrary hole-free expressions, and requires BOTH tail classes to pin the same wildcard value (expression pins have no typed default to guess). It crowns exactly the faithful Match (10 digit arms + `None()` wildcard). Teeth (`tests/phase111_char_guard_table.rs`): fires on the shipped spec; declines conflicting pins, disagreeing tails, an equation-shaped Char spec, and an Int key. Deliberately NOT registered as a `callee_body` denotation — seed-only, the scoped change. A spec-authoring correction rides with it, measured en route: the None side of the contract needs TWO rows (`c >= '0' || output == None()` and `c <= '9' || output == None()`) — the single conjunction-lead row is unparseable, and a disjunctive variant was jointly contradictory, against which the verifier CORRECTLY refuted a faithful body (a spec bug caught by measurement, not a judge bug). **The executed-judge finding:** the battery's adversarial extremes caught `values_equal` (src/synthesis/eval.rs) routing Int/Int equality through f64 — distinct ints within f64 spacing of each other (everything from 2^53 up; at the range top, MIN through MIN+1023 collapse to one f64) compared EQUAL, corrupting both directions of executed judging: a body off by less than the spacing at an extreme would PASS its test, and Phase 109's `require:` evaluation silenced in-domain points (`int_abs` at MIN+1 and MIN+2 judged spec-silent under `x != MIN`). The fix is minimal and general — Int/Int compares exactly before the numeric-promotion path; mixed Int/Float promotion is unchanged — and **no standing verdict moved**: the suites below are baseline + new tests only, in all three configurations. The abs battery (MIN+1/MIN+2 pinned, MIN silent) stands as the regression pin. **`int_gcd` — NAMED BLOCKER, unshipped** (its contract text is preserved verbatim in `tests/phase111_cross_validation.rs`, NOT in `stdlib/int.morph`; the module header names the blocker in one line). The gap is TWO-sided, isolated by measurement: (1) no seed family builds Euclid — the pipeline's seed kinds for the contract are empty and its crown is test-induced Match junk (Inconclusive, 2/6 executed); (2) the statement judge cannot crown even a faithful hand body — Euclid in statement form (abs inlined, Block/Alloc/While) EXECUTES 6/6 against the contract, but with a plain invariant (non-negativity + sum bound) it is **VerificationFailed** against both the full spec and a no-forall variant (the preservation facts are load-bearing even for the boundary rows), and with the full preservation invariant (four leaf-only forall rows over `range(int_abs(a) + int_abs(b) + 1)` + non-negativity + the sum bound) the verdict is **Inconclusive** against both variants — nothing refutes, but Z3 returns Unknown on the quantified divisibility-preservation (forall-over-`%`) obligations, the pattern class Phase 94 explicitly left unmeasured. Closing it needs judge-side work on quantified mod obligations PLUS an Euclid seed family — larger than a minimal seed addition — so under the freeze the entry stays unshipped and returns by **scope amendment (owner decision), proposed here, not taken**. The blocker is pinned in the suite (the entry's absence from the prelude, the body's 6/6 execution, the Inconclusive verdict), so a future judge improvement fails the pin loudly rather than silently changing the record. **Bundle: 769,782 B ≤ 771,072 B budget — headroom 1,290 B, and the trajectory is now a named problem for Phase 112.** The first build measured 772,854 B (over by 1,782): the all-in cost is **≈2,336 B per entry** (12 entries + the seed family over Phase 110's 741,756 B), not the ≈1,010 B Phase 110 projected — the difference is compiled code (the seed family, the shipped-body builders), not source text (12.0 KB of the growth). Source economy recovered 3,072 B — comment discipline plus a compact one-line test format adopted for the library modules from this phase on — to land inside the budget. > **Phase 116 (2026-11-23, branch `feat/stdlib-116-honesty-appendix` from `feat/stdlib-115-list` @ `6645acb`) — CROSS-TARGET HONESTY + BUNDLE FINALIZATION + APPENDIX A REWRITE: the last build phase before the 1.0 gate; clauses 5, 6 and 7 executed as written.** **Clause 5, measured first** (a temporary probe over hand-built candidates, deleted after measurement; the matrix it produced): for a body calling a shipped entry — (a) — **Rust** silently emitted a free call to a function the generated file does not define (`int_abs(x)`, `list_sum(xs)`, `option_unwrap_or(o, 7)`; failure deferred to the user's own rustc, E0425), **C** silently dropped the call (`/* unsupported */;`, the function often left with no return at all), **WAT** emitted a `;; node` comment as the whole body of a result-typed function, **Python** `pass # unsupported` (returns None), **JavaScript** `// unsupported` (returns undefined); only the **IR** debug target named the call faithfully. For the builtin tier — (b), `len` in both IR forms and `int_to_str` — Rust was already correct (`(xs).len() as i64`, `xs.len()`, `(x).to_string()`), and the other four targets silently constant-folded the call in expression position, measured inside the entries' own generated bodies (`list_min`: C `if ((0 == 0))` and For bound `i < 0`, Python `(None == 0)`, JS `(undefined === 0)`). For the closed method table — (c) — no IR form exists: a body-position method call lowers to a Hole before codegen (Rust renders it loudly, TODO + `panic!`; the other targets give it their generic unsupported fallbacks, the standing Hole behaviour for every unlowerable construct, not method-specific), and in spec position only Rust renders spec expressions, the closed table verbatim through `expr_to_rust` (pinned since Phases 77/113; the `'??'` catch-all is unreachable from a checked module). **The fix** (code commit `f9ebace`, all of it at `generate()`'s dispatch, the sole production route): a recursive scan names the body's library involvement (entries = the prelude specs carrying shipped bodies, 29 as they stand; builtins = `len` Call/UnaryOp + `int_to_str` Call). **Rust is correct by construction**: the entries a body uses are emitted into the generated file as real functions — prelude spec + shipped body through `render_rust_function`, factored verbatim out of `generate_rust`, doc head converted `//!` → `///`, transitively closed, the candidate's own name excluded — so the output compiles and runs (the clause's stated measurement; compile+run pinned for Tier-1, Tier-2, Option-entry, two-entry and statement-position callers). **C and WAT refuse loudly**: neither target has a length or aggregate model (C lists are bare pointers; WAT is a scalar i32 model), so entry calls and builtin calls alike fail at generation time with the new `CodegenError::UnrenderableLibraryCall`, naming the call and the target (first offender in name order, deterministic). **Python and JavaScript refuse entry calls** the same way (neither emitter has any call rendering), and **render the builtin tier correctly** in the expression positions their walkers serve — name-keyed, arity-checked arms: Python `len(x)` / `str(x)`, JS `[...(x)].length` (code points for a string, elements for a list — the language's char-count semantics, where `.length` would count UTF-16 units) / `String(x)` — plus statement arms so a discarded builtin call still evaluates, the Rust statement-Call stance. Combinations NOT involving the library keep their standing behaviour byte-for-byte (pinned: a plain sibling call and a plain BinOp body on C/WAT still generate; a non-library call on Python/JS still renders the standing `None`/`undefined`). **Two wider dishonesties measured and recorded as named findings, NOT silently fixed** (this phase is scoped to the clause as written): **NF-116-1** — the non-Rust emitters have no tail renderer (a bare expression body of ANY shape vanishes into the statement catch-all) and skeletal node coverage (Match/Alloc/Index/Assign unserved on several targets), so entry bodies as candidates on C/Python/JS/WAT still render silently-wrong beyond the call combinations fixed here (`char_to_digit` → Python `pass # unsupported`); clause 5's measured floor (generated-Rust compile + run) is met, and per-target entry rendering on those targets is future emitter work for the gate phase to scope. **NF-116-2** — `constraint_to_rust` degrades every `Constraint::Expr` precondition — the parser's only `require:` form — to `true`, so generated Rust precondition asserts assert nothing (`int_clamp`'s `require: lo <= hi` included; method-bearing rows degrade identically — not method-specific); fixing it belongs to a spec-position rendering pass that must also settle spec-position `len`/entry calls in `expr_to_rust`, which today free-calls them, or generated files would stop compiling for len-bearing requires. **Clause 6**: the bundle rebuilds on this tree with the standing build (Binaryen 133, `-Oz --converge`) at **680,280 B ≤ 771,072 B budget — headroom 90,792 B** (pre-pass 844,289 B; +27,484 B over Phase 115's 652,796 B, the honesty machinery and its reachability in the WASM graph); the stdlib asset stands at 33,476 B, unchanged; corpus **16/16 check + 6/6 synthesis** on the rebuilt bundle, not extended (Work Item 1 changed no corpus-relevant behaviour — the corpus exercises check/synthesis, not codegen targets); `budget.txt`'s number untouched, its comment block gains the Phase 116 measurement note per its standing practice. **Clause 7**: Appendix A of `LANGUAGE_REFERENCE.md` is rewritten from "(Planned)" to per-entry reality — every shipped entry with signature, tier (Builtin / Tier-1 Verified / Tier-2 executed-exact), semantics and one example; > **Phase 118 (2026-11-23, branch `docs/embed-118-audit` from master @ `7cd2920`) — 1.1 EMBEDDABLE AUDIT: feasibility + scope for the Embeddable Morphic milestone, measured in [`EMBED_AUDIT.md`](EMBED_AUDIT.md) (the Phase 106/99 lineage: measurement + design only, no production code changed, nothing published, no package uploaded; the only code is the probe artifact `tests/phase118_probes.rs`, 12 probes, committed ahead of the document).** **Headline verdict: 1.1 is achievable as ratified, but its centre of gravity is not where the Phase 105 sketch assumed — neither named seed is load-bearing as it stands.** **The JS codegen target cannot yet emit a single shipped library body that runs** (NF-116-1 measured at the exact boundary 1.1 cares about; generated output graded with node v24): the Tier-1 `int_abs` generates a function with **no `return` at all** (`int_abs(-5) === undefined` at runtime — the JS walker has no tail renderer, and bare-expression bodies vanish wholesale, `string_is_empty` included despite `len`'s correct expression arm); the Tier-2 `list_sum` partially renders and **throws** (`ReferenceError: acc is not defined` — Alloc/Assign are `// unsupported` while `return acc;` survives); Match bodies (`option_unwrap_or`, `char_to_digit`) vanish; `%` and `<=` render a bare `?` (`return (x ? 2);` — a **SyntaxError**, unparseable); constructors, list literals and Index render `undefined`; Int literals render as bare JS numbers (the i64 maximum is emitted digit-exact and parsed by JS as 2^63). The asymmetry Phase 116 left is the framing: entry *calls* refuse loudly on JS while the entries' own *bodies* silently break — Phase 116's clause was about calls, 1.1 is about bodies, so **the JS emitter completion is 1.1's first build phase (priced L, embeddable subset)**. **`crates/morphic-wasm/` is a playground shell, not an embedding surface**: five exports, all whole-source-in / JSON-string-out (`check(source: string): string` is the typed surface), one of them a Phase 65 timing probe still riding in the public API; a three-step hand-duplicated init (async bindgen init → host fetches the 33,476 B asset itself → install-once `init_stdlib`, a second install an error); the bundle is 680,280 B + 16,680 B glue for the whole compiler; and the v0.6 D2 cap stands — **no Z3 in the browser build means no Verified verdicts at runtime** (`verification_available: false`), so verified functions must be synthesized natively and shipped as artifacts. **The route that carries the milestone is pre-generation** (synthesize + verify at build time, ship the generated code), with the 29 entries as the first package's contents: Rust generation is real today (all 29 entries as standalone generated Rust files sum to **37,149 B** of source), and a Tier-2 entry's tier survives generation today only as its `doc:` comment — the binding layer must carry it into typings + a machine-readable manifest (gate-sketch clause 4). **The Rust API** is the whole compiler uncurated (seven public modules; `api` has no call-a-function entry point — the probe measures that `eval` + `shipped_body` compose at IR level: `int_abs`/`int_clamp`/`list_sum` answer correctly through a hand-built `Env`, a mechanism, not an API), and the crate is not publish-ready (CLI-grade default features pulling `reqwest`/`indicatif`; the `z3` crate's `gh-release` build-time download, which also defeats docs.rs; no readme/keywords/categories; the whole internal surface nominally under the declared SemVer). **Type mapping**: exact for Rust across the 1.0 surface; for TypeScript a decision list — Int is `number` (lossy past 2^53; float `/`; `%` unrendered) vs `bigint` (exact, and its `/`/`%` semantics match Morphic Int's), Char/String carry code-point-vs-UTF-16 length semantics (the Phase 116 `len` arm already chose code points), and **Option/Result have no representation in generated code at all** (constructors → `undefined`, which also disqualifies `T | undefined` for Option — `Some(x)` and `None` would be indistinguishable). **NF-116-2** is priced into the Rust-crate phase (the generated `int_abs` carries `debug_assert!(true, "Precondition violated")` verbatim — a documentation-grade defect on the "verified function" claim). **Registry facts, verified live 2026-11-23**: the unscoped npm name `morphic` is **taken** (unrelated package, since 2015, latest 1.0.16); the crates.io name `morphic` is **free** (the API, with a proper User-Agent, returns "crate `morphic` does not exist" — the bare endpoint's 403 is its bot policy, checked and resolved). **Packaging**: npm-via-generated-source is Route A (the bindgen build stays the playground's; the 1.1 package is generated `.js` + `.d.ts` + manifest under a scoped name); the **Component Model** is priced honestly — it dissolves most of §3's losses at the boundary (WIT has `s64`/`option`/`result`/records natively) but from here it is a new crate + WIT world + second pipeline with no toolchain in the tree (**XL as the 1.1 route, M–L later**, with §3's decisions transferring unchanged), and the audit recommends deferring it in the open as the post-1.1 Disebar step rather than pretending the npm package ends the distribution story. **The 5-minute quickstart draft grades 0 of 5 steps working today** (install: no package + name taken; import: no module assembly — `morphic build` emits one function to one file; typed call: JS doesn't run + no `.d.ts` is generated from any spec; Option and Result: no representation), each failure naming a priced phase. **Dependencies: 1.1 needs none of G4** (all entries are first-order; its absence caps only higher-order entries and host callbacks, both outside the ratified scope), **§3.9** (embedding consumes executed artifacts; its absence caps the *label*, handled by honesty machinery, and its landing later upgrades labels without changing bytes), **or quantified-mod** (`int_gcd` already stands out per Amendment 1). **The audit delivers:** a 7-clause 1.1 gate sketch in the M1 style (frozen package surface / host-executed exactness in clean projects / type honesty / verification honesty with tiers in the package surface / the timed 5-minute test / budgets / documentation) with a closing line, a phase plan **119–125** (ratify + freeze · JS emitter completion · typed bindings · package assembly + npm publish · Rust crate route · quickstart + guide · gate run + merge + v1.1.0; > **Phase 120 (2026-11-23, branch `feat/embed-120-js-emitter` from `feat/embed-119-scope` @ `a056596`) — JAVASCRIPT EMITTER COMPLETION, the embeddable subset (EMBED_SCOPE §5, D5a): the Phase 118 grading is answered arm by arm, and the freeze's exit condition for this phase is met — every one of the 29 shipped bodies generates JavaScript that parses and answers its frozen battery correctly under node.** The work is one file (`src/codegen/mod.rs`) plus pins. **Cascade check first, as the brief required:** the JS emitter is native-only — the synthesized artifact classifies only target-name routing (`rust_target_route`: "javascript"/"js" → route 4), never JS node forms, and `generate_synthesized` routes non-Rust targets back to native `generate` — so both build configurations share this emitter byte-for-byte, the artifact is untouched, and the bootstrap suite stands at the same counts as the default suite (the configuration-independence is measured, not assumed). **What landed — three renderers** mirroring the Rust walker's contexts (statements / tail / expressions) over a kind environment (`JsEnv`: spec parameter types, `Alloc` types, literal shapes; block-scoped clones at braced arms): the **tail renderer** itself (the missing piece — a bare expression body returns its value; `int_abs` answers numbers again); **statement arms** Let (`const`), Alloc (`let`), Assign, While (with the invariant carried as a comment, Rust parity), For (the interpreter evaluates bounds once, so the end is hoisted into the init; the loop variable is a BigInt), Loop (`while (true)`), Break (plain in statement loops; a tail Loop's valued Break is the function's return — the interpreter's value-carrying loop), Match (a discrimination chain over a scrutinee temp, wrapped in a bare block so sibling Matches cannot redeclare it), TryPropagate (the Result-only temp form: an Err payload unwinds as the return), statement-position Append (the interpreter rebinds: `+=` on a String cell, `.push` on a List cell), and bare expression statements; **expression arms** If (ternary), Match/Block/Let/Loop/While/For in IIFE form with the tail renderer inside, Index, constructors, list literals, Assign-as-expression, and the full operator set the bodies use — **Mod/Le/Ge land** (the bare `?` is gone), Xor renders `!==` (Bool-only in the interpreter; a `^` would coerce), Shl/Shr ride BigInt shifts; unary Neg/Not/Abs/Len/Clone (Clone is the Phase 91 identity). **Int is BigInt end-to-end (D3a):** literals carry the `n` suffix (the i64 maximum reads back digit-exact; the 2^53 cliff is closed), BigInt `/` and `%` are Morphic Int's own truncating semantics, comparisons are exact, and `len` yields `BigInt([...(x)].length)` — the Phase 116 code-point spread form, now Int-valued at the boundary; `int_to_str` stays `String(x)`, exact over BigInt. **Option/Result are the D4a shapes (D4a):** `Some(x)` renders the payload itself, `None` renders `null`, `Ok`/`Err` render the discriminated-union objects, and Match discriminates on exactly those forms (null test / tag test) with payload binding — a generated function's inputs and outputs ARE the package-boundary shapes Phase 121 will type. Any other capitalized constructor takes a consistent generic tagged form (`{ tag, values }`), with Match discriminating on it the same way. One correctness fix rides along: Char/String literals are **escaped** now — the old interpolation emitted a raw newline for a `'\n'` Char literal, a SyntaxError inside `char_is_whitespace`'s own body. **The entry-call reconciliation (the brief's work item 4):** `generate()` no longer refuses entry calls on the JS route; they render as **plain calls to the entry's export name**, the form Phase 121's module assembly satisfies by generating the entries into the same module. The reconciliation is deliberate and recorded at the dispatch and in the Phase 116 comment block: the enforcement's purpose was killing silent wrongness, and a call the package assembly provably satisfies is the correct-by-construction case — proven here by hand-assembling a caller with its entry and running it under node. Python keeps refusing (its emitter has no call rendering; Python as a package target is outside 1.1 per EMBED §7); C/WAT are unchanged. At this phase's level a sibling (non-entry) user-function call is indistinguishable from an unknown name at the `generate()` boundary, so both keep the standing fallback (`undefined` / the standing comment) — module context is Phase 121's assembly concern, recorded here so the line is visible. **The node battery (the exit measurement):** `tests/phase120_js_emitter.rs` (18 tests) generates each shipped body, writes the module plus a driver into a temp dir, and executes the frozen Phase 111/112/115 cross-validation points under node v24 in their §3 JS forms — **1,045 pinned points at 100% agreement** (Int 102, Char 606 = 6 × the 101-point sweep, String/Result/Option 88, List 249) **plus `list_binary_search`'s 67-point property battery** (result `null` iff absent; a returned index always names the target; the 64 unique-target points pin the index exactly, the 3 duplicate-target points are index-silent as frozen). Spec-silent points are excluded exactly as the batteries record them (R3: `int_abs` at the Int minimum, `int_clamp`'s inverted ranges). **Plausible winners, same treatment:** Euclid's While body (Alloc + While + inner Alloc + Assign + Mod, invariant comment included), a valued-Break Loop in tail position and a bare-Break Loop in statement position, a statement-position Match over Option with Assign arms, the lexeme shape (a String accumulator grown by Append of indexed chars — code-point indexing, so "héllo" round-trips exactly), a counting For (the count_matching shape), and Let chains — all run correctly under node. **Pins flipped at their sites:** the nine Phase 118 JS probes (re-aimed at the completed emitter, the file's header recording the closure), the Phase 116 honesty pin (split: Python refuses loudly, JS renders — the builtins pin survives unchanged, its substring assertions holding inside the BigInt `len` form), and the in-module Phase 77 record pin (the JS RecordLit field now renders `0n` per D3a). **Named boundaries, recorded not silently expanded:** aggregate equality is JS reference equality (`===` on arrays/objects) — scalar equality is exact and no frozen battery point uses aggregate equality, and the audit's inventory does not list it; a Break/Return inside an expression-position IIFE renders as that IIFE's return rather than propagating to the enclosing loop/function as the interpreter does (no measured body carries the shape); Guard patterns render as never-matching arms (the interpreter declines guarded arms when tested, so no judged point can reach one); Append/Index on a base whose kind the environment cannot know take the List/spread resp. direct-index forms (a known String base gets the code-point Index form); Set/Map collections, `Merge`, and the interpreter-declined unary forms (Head/Tail/Init/Last/Reverse) keep the standing `undefined` fallback — none can appear in a judged body. **Bundle:** the completed emitter is reachable in the WASM graph; the playground bundle rebuilds at **698,714 B ≤ the standing 771,072 B budget** (headroom 72,358 B; `playground/budget.txt` untouched; the stdlib asset unmoved at 33,476 B). Suites: **697/0/30 default, 697/0/30 bootstrap-codegen, 564/0/22 no-Z3** (baselines 678/678/545 + 19 new teeth: the 18 Phase 120 tests and the Phase 116 split's second half). No merge — Phase 121 (typed bindings + the tier manifest) proceeds from this branch against the freeze.

Entry-to-entry calls resolve inside the module by construction; measured, no shipped body calls another entry (the bodies' only calls are the `len` builtin, 3 sites, rendered by the emitter's arms) — the entries call each other in *constraint* rows, which are spec-side, not body-side. **One source of truth:** declarations and manifest both derive from the input specs — signatures by `morphic_signature` (the §2.1 form: `T → R`, `(T, U) → R`), types by `ts_type` (§3: Int → `bigint`, Char → `string`, List → `T[]`, Option → `T | null` with union operands parenthesized, Result → the discriminated union verbatim) — and the manifest pin asserts each row's signature equals the mechanically rendered one, so drift between the two artifacts is impossible by construction and checked anyway. **Wrappers: measured NONE.** The brief left the wrapper question open per export; the measurement is that Phase 120's generated functions already speak the §3 boundary shapes natively (BigInt arithmetic, payload-or-`null` Option, tagged-union Result, one-code-point Char strings), so every frozen export is declared over its raw generated function and the generator carries no wrapper machinery — the pin holds the assembled module to exactly the 29 definitions and 29 exports (no helper, no shim, no extra name), and the clean-host battery runs typed §3-shaped values against the raw functions. **The manifest pin** holds all 29 rows in exact correspondence with §2.1: names, frozen signatures, tiers, verdict bases, `doc` verbatim from each entry's spec, and the battery counts of the standing Phase 111/112/115 cross-validation batteries — `pinned` = exactly-pinned points (Int 102, Char 606, String/Result/Option 88, List 249 + `list_binary_search`'s 64 exactly-pinned property points) and `specSilent` = the recorded spec-silent points (`int_abs` 1 at the Int minimum, `int_clamp` 2 on inverted ranges, `list_binary_search` 3 duplicate-target indices; zero elsewhere; the search battery's 67 property points thus split 64 + 3). Package fields: `@thvtzy/morphic`, `packageVersion` = `morphicVersion` = the generating crate's version (1.0.0 on this tree; 1.1.0 at the release by the R6 lockstep), `scope` = `EMBED_SCOPE.md`. **Artifact sizes, for Phase 122's budget measurement:** module 12,499 B, declarations 10,901 B, manifest 12,509 B — the manifest runs ~2× its §4 bracket (6,200 B) because each row carries its entry's full doc text verbatim (the bracket assumed ~200 B/row; a negative control — the same import with a `string`-typed binding and `number` arguments — is rejected, so the strictness is measured, not assumed. **The clean host project** (a scratch directory outside the repo tree, `{"type": "module"}`) imports the assembled module and calls seven representative exports with typed values at frozen battery points under node — `int_clamp` (Tier-1 Int, 13 points), `char_to_digit` (Char, the full 101-point alphabet), `option_unwrap_or` (28) + `option_ok_or` (9), `result_unwrap_or` (36), `list_sum` + `list_min` (Tier-2 List, 15 each) — **217 points, 100% agreement**, BigInt values crossing the test boundary as decimal strings and re-encoded canonically for comparison. **The ungated generator (D1a):** the same `generate_bindings` binds a user module — the sample spec `absolute` (int_abs's guarded-row shape under a user name) is crowned by the production pipeline stages in the test, and its manifest row carries exactly the standing that run measured: **Verified under Z3 in the default and bootstrap configurations (tier-1 / z3-verified — minted by the pipeline, not the generator)**, executed-exact in the no-Z3 configuration by the same dynamic comparison (the pin asserts row == measured standing in whichever configuration runs it, so a no-Z3 route can never mint the Verified claim, R12); its generated JS answers the spec's 3 points under node and its declaration is the §3 shape. **Suites: 704/0/30 default, 704/0/30 bootstrap-codegen, 571/0/22 no-Z3** (baselines 697/697/564 + exactly the 7 new teeth in every configuration). > **Phase 123 (2026-11-23, branch `feat/embed-123-rust-facade` from `feat/embed-122-npm-package` @ `aadaef0`) — RUST FACADE CRATE (EMBED_SCOPE §5, D7a; dry-run only per R5): the freeze's exit conditions are met for the assembly, the standalone build, the docs build and the packaging — and the phase closes with ONE NAMED BLOCKER, measured in the host rehearsal: `char_to_digit` does not stand at its battery in generated Rust (the Char-pattern widening, below); gate clause 2 cannot pass for the crate until one of the two priced routes lands.** The work is a new assembly module (`src/codegen/facade.rs`), the CLI surface `morphic build --facade`, nine pins (`tests/phase123_rust_facade.rs`), and the assembled crate itself, checked in at its repo home **`packages/rust/`** (7 files, 50,909 B — the crate carries no size budget, R8). **Placement + naming, resolved against the repo's actual layout:** the root package IS `morphic` — the compiler, which D7a keeps unpublished — and cargo forbids two same-named packages in one workspace; the facade is therefore its own workspace root (its generated `Cargo.toml` carries an empty `[workspace]` table), the standard shape for a separately publishable crate inside a larger repo. The crates.io name is carried by the facade alone; no rename was needed and none was improvised. **Generation:** each function is rendered from its shipped body by the very renderer the Phase 116 Rust route uses (`render_rust_function`), its `//!` file head re-carried as the function's rustdoc with the §2.4 prose (the entry's doc verbatim — with one rustdoc link escape, the `i` of `xs[i]`, measured as the single rustdoc warning over the frozen docs — plus tier, verdict basis and battery lines); bodies byte-identical to the pipeline's rendering, nothing transcribed. The manifest comes from Phase 121's generator under this package's name (a pin holds the crate's rows exactly equal to the npm package's, only the `package` field differing) and is addressable in-crate as `morphic::MANIFEST_JSON`. The generated module carries scoped lint allowances for the three stylistic lints the emitter's uniform style trips (measured at this phase: 51 warnings over the 29 functions — `unused_parens` ×40, `unreachable_patterns` ×10, `unused_mut` ×1), so the crate builds warning-free without a second transcription of the bodies. **Regeneration discipline (clause 4's machinery):** the checked assembly (`assemble_rust_facade_checked`) re-runs the crowning surface shared with the npm assembly (`package::verify_crowns`) before generating and refuses by name on a moved crown (the full checked run took ~25 s); two assemblies are byte-identical, and the checked-in crate is pinned byte-equal to a fresh assembly. **The version mechanic (R6)** is the npm one's: the crate version is stamped from the compiler crate's version (1.0.0 on this tree), so Phase 125's 1.1.0 is one version edit + one re-assembly. **NF-116-2 — TAKEN at this crate's surface (R9):** the three frozen preconditions render genuinely — `int_abs` asserts `(x != ((0 - 9223372036854775807) - 1))`, `int_clamp` asserts `(lo <= hi)`, `list_binary_search` asserts `list_is_sorted(xs.clone())` (the clone rule: the assert is a proposition and must not consume the argument — a call argument that is a plain variable of a non-Copy parameter type clones at assert position) — in the standing Phase 55 form (`debug_assert!` under `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`), pinned verbatim; no `debug_assert!(true` placeholder stands anywhere in the crate, and the compiled harness's three `should_panic` tests prove the asserts fire on out-of-domain calls (the R3 contract). The renderer is facade-local (`facade_constraint_to_rust`: Expr/Predicate/Eq/Order/And/Or/Not/Implies recursive; quantified rows keep the placeholder — no frozen entry carries one, pinned). **The residue, named in the open:** the compiler's general Rust emitter keeps the placeholder — `constraint_to_rust` is mirrored by the self-host Codegen spec's equations and the synthesized emitter renders through them (the M3 corpus holds the two byte-equal), so the global fix is a lockstep cascade of the Phase 113 shape, not absorbed here; the crate's docs and README state both halves. **THE BLOCKER — the Char-pattern widening (finding F4's caveat, standing since the M4 gate):** the clean-host rehearsal ran ALL 29 entries against their full frozen batteries (the Phase 111/112/115 point sets, expectations by their own mirrors) and stands at **28/29** — every Int, Char-classifier, String, Result/Option and List entry agrees 100% in generated Rust — except `char_to_digit`, whose shipped body is a Match over Char literal patterns (the Phase 111 `char_guard_table` crown) and whose generated form widens all eleven arms to `_` (`ir_pattern_to_rust` renders Int/Bool/String literal patterns literally; Char falls to its `_` catch-all, in lockstep with the synthesized emitter). The M2 specs are written in the parser's actually-supported dialect, documented in their file headers. Wiring the older examples into `check` (or fixing the parser gaps) is future work, separate from M2.

> **Synthesis run (2026-11-20, branch `m2-synthesis-run`):** all 14 M2 specs were run through the real pipeline (parse → typecheck → synthesize → Z3 `verify_all` → `select_best` → codegen) via the test-only probe in `src/m2_synthesis_probe.rs` (`cargo test -- --ignored --nocapture m2_synthesis_probe`; generated winners are written to `target/m2-synthesis/`). Only opt level 1 can run: it is the sole LLM-free configuration. Opt levels 2–4 set `use_llm = true` and fail immediately in `seed_population` with `LlmError("No LLM backend enabled")` — the default build compiles neither LLM feature (`llm-local` / `llm-remote`), and no Ollama server exists in this environment (verified via CLI `build -O 2` / `-O 3` and locked in by the unit test `synthesis_opt3_blocked_without_llm_backend`). Candidate counts and times below are from one probe run; both vary between runs (randomized engine), while the Z3 verdicts and winner provenance were identical across 3 runs.

> **Why the run cannot close the gate — root causes, all verified in the code:**
> 1. **The Z3 stage is candidate-independent.** `Verifier::verify_one` (`src/verify/verifier.rs`) encodes only the spec's postconditions; the candidate body is never encoded (`is_well_formed` is a stub returning `true`). Its encoder maps boolean-valued subexpressions to int `0` (`encode_expr_int` fallback) and any `Or`-rooted formula to `true` (`encode_expr_bool` fallback), so the verdict is decided by constraint *syntax*: guard-style (`||`) lookup constraints always hold, `output == <bool expr>` equations never hold. The 4 "Verified" specs above are exactly the guard-style ones — a property of the spec text, identical for every candidate, not evidence that a synthesized implementation is correct.
> 2. **The search never executes tests.** `evaluate_candidate` (`src/synthesis/engine.rs`) returns `test_pass_ratio = 1.0` unconditionally and a constant `constraint_score = 0.7`; ranking is driven by AST-shape heuristics (depth/size) only.
> 3. **Winners keep their holes.** The test-induced seed's wildcard arm is a `Hole` and no pipeline stage fills it (the template builders also return bare holes); codegen renders holes as `panic!("Hole not filled")`. 13/14 winners carry ≥ 1 hole.
> 4. **Rust codegen defects (overlaps M3).** Spec test names are emitted verbatim as Rust fn identifiers — hyphens make 12/14 generated files unparseable; `Match` bodies are emitted as statements whose arm values are discarded (`value;`), which is E0308 once names are sanitized (proven on `is_literal_kind` and `node_kind_name`); unsupported IR in expression position becomes `/* UNSUPPORTED */` and unknown calls become `_()` (the two Mutation winners). Net: **0/14 generated files compile**, so 0/14 can be executed against their spec tests or cross-validated against the `tests/m2_proof.rs` mirrors.
>
> **Remaining for the M2 gate:** (a) an LLM backend (feature + server) or a scorer that actually executes spec tests, so the M1 pipeline shape (LLM seed → MCTS → Z3 → codegen) can run as described; (b) a verifier that encodes/evaluates the candidate itself, so "Verified" is a statement about the implementation; (c) the codegen fixes in (4) plus hole filling, so generated code compiles; only then (d) cross-validation against the mirrors. Until (a)–(c) land, "Same validation pipeline as M1" and the M2 gate stay unchecked — deliberately, per-spec evidence above.
>

Re-running the probe and compiling every winner with `rustc --edition 2021 --crate-type lib`: **8/14 compile** (was 0/14), **0/14 compile free of hole/unsupported markers** — every winner in this run still carries ≥ 1 hole (12× 1 hole, `needs_parens` 2, `tags_compatible` 3). The 6 remaining failures split into: 2 files (`needs_parens`, `tags_compatible`, the Mutation winners) still on defect (4c) — `_()` in an `if` condition does not parse; and 4 String-returning files (`binop_symbol`, `node_kind_name`, `print_node_kind`, `type_tag_name`) on a newly exposed defect (4d): `IRLiteral::String` is emitted as a `&str` literal while the spec return type is `String` (E0308) — previously masked by the `value;` discard. Fixing (4d), (4c), and hole filling (root cause 3) remains open, so item (c) above is only partially done.

> **Codegen fix follow-up 2 (2026-11-20, branch `fix/codegen-output-2`):** defect (4d) is FIXED with regression tests — codegen now threads the expected type to the emission points that know one (`ir_to_rust_expr_typed`: the spec return type for match arms and `Return` expressions, an `Alloc`'s declared type, a `Typed` node's own annotation), and only there is a string literal emitted owned (`"s".to_string()`); everywhere else it stays a `&str`, guarded by a negative test. Re-running the probe and compiling every winner as above: **12/14 compile** (was 8/14 — all 4 String-returning files now compile), **0/14 compile free of hole/unsupported markers** (unchanged: every winner in this run still carries exactly 1 hole, so the hole `panic!` marker remains in all 14; hole filling is root cause 3, still open). Defect (4c) is now diagnosed precisely and is NOT a codegen defect: the `_()` in the earlier run's `if` conditions is `IRNode::Call { function: "_", args: [] }`, emitted verbatim by codegen — the node itself is manufactured by the engine's random tree generator (`random_ir_tree`, `src/synthesis/engine.rs`, arm 3) as a placeholder leaf, a sibling of the real `Hole` leaves the same generator produces. It is an unfilled node in function position (engine territory, root cause 3 family); no function named `_` exists in any spec, template, or builtin, so there is nothing for codegen to emit — the fix belongs to the engine (stop generating placeholder calls, or fill them), and codegen was deliberately left unchanged for it. Variance note: winner shapes are randomized per run — in this run the two Mutation winners (`needs_parens`, `tags_compatible`) contained no `_()` at all and instead failed on E0425 (`return result;` after a `Hole` — the `Var("result")` leaf is another `random_ir_tree`/`random_filling` artifact). Item (c) above remains partially done: what is left is hole filling and the engine-side placeholder nodes.

> **Engine placeholder + hole-ranking follow-up (2026-11-20, branch `fix/engine-placeholders`):** defect (4c) is FIXED at the source — `random_ir_tree` arm 3 now emits an honest `Hole` instead of `Call { function: "_", args: [] }` (regression test: property sweep over generated trees asserting no `Call` to `"_"`; zero `_()` in every winner file since). Holes also cost something for the first time: `evaluate_candidate` decays correctness credit (`test_pass_ratio`, `constraint_score`) ×0.5 per hole in the body, and `select_best` hard-gates — if any hole-free candidate exists, a holed candidate cannot win; only when none exists does selection fall back to ranking the holed pool (unit tests cover both branches). Re-running the probe 3× and compiling every winner as above: **winner holes collapsed from 14× exactly 1 (every prior run) to 14× 0, 14× 0, and 13× 0 + 1× 1** — the single holed winner (`node_arity`, run 3) is the fallback case: no hole-free candidate reached its verified pool that run. **Compiles went DOWN: 0/14, 0/14, 1/14 (was 12/14); compiles free of hole/unsupported markers 0/14 (unchanged).** That is a change in *which* candidates win, not a codegen regression: the previously compiling winners were tidy trees carrying one hole, while the hole-free winners now crowned come from the random/Mutation family and fail on the next layer of generator artifacts — stray `Var("result")` leaves (E0425; the `random_ir_tree` arm 0 / `random_filling` family flagged in follow-up 2), unbound `a`/`b` vars (E0425), E0308 type mismatches, and `return` in statement position. Net: hole filling is no longer the binding constraint — the population produces hole-free candidates for nearly every spec — candidate *quality* is. The generator invents names that are never bound, and evaluation still cannot execute spec tests to tell a correct hole-free tree from a nonsensical one. Next blockers, in order: (1) stop the generator emitting free-variable leaves (`Var("result")`/`Var("output")` where nothing binds them) or bind them at codegen; (2) a scorer that actually executes spec tests (root cause (a) above), so ranking rewards correctness, not just completeness. Item (c) stays partially done. Suite after this branch: 89 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored.

> **Engine test-execution follow-up (2026-11-20, branch `feat/engine-test-execution`):** blocker (2) above is FIXED — the engine now has a truth signal. New module `src/synthesis/eval.rs`: a total IR interpreter for the expression subset (Literal/Var/BinOp/UnaryOp with numeric promotion, If, Match over literal/variable/wildcard patterns, Let, Block, Return, `len` + the `List[...]` literal call, Collection/Index, Typed). Everything outside the subset — Hole, loops, Alloc/Assign, lambdas, Map/Filter/Fold/Sort, unknown calls (including template pseudo-calls like `first`/`rest`), guard patterns — returns `NotEvaluable` with a reason; the interpreter never panics and never guesses. No evaluator existed before (the only matches for "eval" in the tree were `evaluate_candidate` itself). Spec tests turned out to be directly usable: `Test.input`/`expected_output` are AST `Expr`s, mapped to evaluator values by `value_of_expr` (literals directly; composites lowered through the engine's own `expr_to_ir`, the same conversion `seed_from_tests` uses). Single-param specs bind the input value to the parameter; multi-param specs would need a List input of matching arity — in practice they carry no `.morph` tests at all, so nothing is lost today. `evaluate_candidate` now measures `test_pass_ratio = passed / evaluable` by actually running the candidate body (`run_spec_tests`), still ×0.5 per hole; a body that cannot be evaluated on a test FAILS that test, while a test that cannot be *mapped* is excluded from the denominator. Specs with tests but zero mappable ones keep the legacy structural score, marked `FALLBACK` in code; test-less specs keep the neutral 0.5. Decisive tests: a hand-built correct `is_literal_kind` candidate scores exactly 1.0, an always-false one exactly 2/3, an unbound-`Var("result")` body 0.0, and the TestInduced match shape (1 wildcard Hole) scores measured 1.0 × 0.5 hole decay = 0.5. Probe (3 runs, `winner_tpr` is the new probe field): all 42 winners Mutation, all hole-free; **measured winner tpr is 0.000 in 34/42** — the signal's first verdict is that the crowned winners are semantically wrong, including several Z3-verified ones (`node_arity`, `type_tag_name`, `node_kind_name`, `binop_symbol`: verified 13–20/13–20 yet tpr 0.000 in most runs — the Z3 constraint encoding and actual test behavior still tell different stories). Non-zero glimpses exist (`is_known_type_tag` 0.600, `line_width_ok` 0.667, `node_arity` 0.400, `is_infix_kind` 0.333 in individual runs) but no winner reached 1.0, and run-3 winners still compile 0/14. `tags_compatible`/`needs_parens` sit at the 0.500 no-tests neutral in every run, as designed. Why truth does not yet crown winners: the composite score still gives a flat placeholder `constraint_score` 0.7 to every hole-free body, and the GA's 10 generations can lose the TestInduced seed (which would measure 0.5 after hole decay) before final scoring — ranking now *can* tell correct from compiling-random, but selection pressure is not yet dominated by it. Next blockers, in order: (1) generator free-variable leaves (`Var("result")`/`Var("output")`) — still the compile killer; (2) make measured tpr dominate selection (revisit composite weights / the placeholder constraint score, and protect the TestInduced seed through the GA); (3) reconcile Z3 verification with executed behavior. Suite after this branch: 106 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored.
>
> **Engine truth-selection follow-up (2026-11-20, branch `fix/engine-truth-selection`):** blockers (1) and (2) above are FIXED. (1) Generation is scope-aware: `random_ir_tree` threads a scope (spec parameters; its own `For` variable extends it in the loop body) and draws `Var` leaves only from it via `random_scoped_leaf` (literal fallback when empty); a new `scope_at_path` walks a hole's path collecting enclosing binders (`Let`/`For`/Lambda/Closure/match-pattern), and `random_filling` + `generate_hole_fillings` — which hardcoded `Var("result")`/`Var("output")` and `Var("x")` / `a + b` — now draw only from that scope. Property test: every `Var` in generated trees must be in scope (failed before: `Var("result")` with scope `[]`). (2) Measured truth dominates selection: `composite_score` weights are now 0.85 tpr / 0.05 constraint / 0.05 complexity / 0.05 quality, so a tpr gap of ≥0.25 (worth 0.2125) always beats the maximum combined swing of the other dimensions (0.15); `mcts_evaluate`'s private copy of the old weights now calls `composite_score`, so the invariant holds for the MCTS reward, GA fitness, `score_and_rank`, and `verify_all`'s re-scoring alike. And the TestInduced seed is protected: `run()` snapshots it after seeding and re-admits it just before final scoring if the search dropped it (structural presence via Debug fingerprint — `IRNode` has no `PartialEq`); it is re-scored on the same footing as everyone else, and winning is still earned (the completeness gate still bars the holed seed when a hole-free candidate exists). A unit test locks the seed's presence in the synthesized pool for `is_literal_kind` at its measured tpr 0.5. Probe (3 runs, same method as above): all 42 winners Mutation, all hole-free — unchanged. **Winner tpr 0.000: 29/42 (was 34/42); non-zero winners 13/42 (was 8/42); max still 0.667, none reached 1.0.** Directionally consistent with the mechanism (the pool is now sorted tpr-first, so criteria ties in `select_best` break toward measured truth), but modest — treat as movement, not proof. **Compiles: 0/14, 0/14, 0/14 — the count did not move, the failure class did: E0425 (free variables) now occurs in 0 of 42 winner files** (the class is gone from winners entirely); 40 files fail E0308 (type mismatch — e.g. a `vec![]` body for a Bool spec, `0;` as an i64 body) and 1 fails E0069. Generation is now scope-valid but still not type-directed. Why winners still measure 0 for most specs — the search itself, in order: (a) the MCTS explores a *single* root — the first node is initialized from one random population member and selection never starts another root, so the harvest is ~10–20 completions of one usually-random member, and completions of the TestInduced seed (whose wildcard hole any menu filling would complete into a test-passing, hole-free body) almost never enter the pool; (b) the variation operators are stubs — 4 of 6 mutation kinds are no-ops, `random_subtree` returns a whole-tree clone so crossover swaps nothing — at opt level 1 there is effectively no variation engine beyond MCTS hole filling; (c) with (a)+(b), the hole-free pool for most specs contains no candidate passing even one test, so tpr-dominant ranking has nothing true to crown, and the gate (by design) keeps the 0.5-tpr holed seed from winning. Next blockers, in order: (1) make the MCTS harvest completions of *every* population member (or at least every seed), not one random root; (2) real mutation operators (subtree replacement that actually selects a subtree; the no-op stubs filled in); (3) type-directed generation/selection so bodies are at least type-plausible for the spec's return type; (4) reconcile Z3 verification with executed behavior (carried over). Suite after this branch: 114 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored.

> **Engine seed-harvest follow-up (2026-11-20, branch `feat/mcts-seed-harvest`):** blocker (1) above is FIXED — and fixing it exposed a deeper one underneath. Two changes. (a) `replace_at_path`, the walker under `replace_hole` (used by MCTS expansion AND rollout), implemented only the `Block` path step; every other `PathElem` (`MatchCase`, `IfThen`/`IfElse`, `LetBody`, `BinOp*`, …) fell into a no-op arm, so a hole anywhere except under pure `Block` nesting was silently left in place: expansion children were still-holed clones of their parent (never terminal, never harvested) and rollouts could not fill such holes either. It now mirrors `scope_at_path`'s traversal for every variant (unit test covers `MatchCase`/`IfElse`/`LetBody`/nested paths; failed before, at the match arm). This retroactively corrects the Phase-3/8 picture of the harvest: with the walker broken, MCTS contributed ~nothing and the crowned "Mutation" winners were effectively raw random seeds. (b) The MCTS now roots a tree at the TestInduced seed too: the per-tree loop/harvest was extracted to `mcts_harvest_tree(root, kind)`; `mcts_search` runs it at one random member (pass 1, as before) and once per holed TestInduced seed (pass 2, provenance `mutation_kind: "mcts_seed_harvest"`), so seed completions enter the final pool deterministically rather than when the seed happened to be the random root (~1 in 20 runs). Evidence chain for the new pipeline test (the pool returned by `synthesize(is_literal_kind, 1)` contains a hole-free seed completion measuring tpr 1.0): failed 5/5 before either fix, still failed 3/3 with (a) alone, passes 5/5 with both. Probe (3 runs, same method): **winner tpr 1.000 in 36/42 — every tested spec in every run; winner tpr 0.000: 0/42 (was 29/42); the remaining 6 are `tags_compatible`/`needs_parens` at the 0.500 no-tests neutral, as designed.** All 42 winners hole-free, all Mutation provenance. **Compiles: 1/14 in each run (was 0/14)** — `node_arity` in all three runs; the other 39 files fail E0308 (37×) or E0069 (2×), and E0425 remains 0/42. The new winners are visibly the seed completions (per-test match arms verbatim), and the compile blocker is now precisely located: the wildcard arm's filling is type-blind — `is_literal_kind` (returns Bool) gets `_ => 0`, `type_tag_name` (returns String) gets `_ => 0` — behaviorally unreachable by the spec's tests, so the interpreter honestly scores it 1.0, but rustc rejects the arm's type. The hole even carries `expected_type: Some(return_type)`; nothing reads it. Next blockers, in order: (1) type-directed fillings — `generate_hole_fillings`/`random_filling` must draw from the hole's expected type; this is now THE compile blocker for otherwise-correct winners, and fixing it should take most of the 12 tested specs from tpr-1.0-but-uncompilable to tpr-1.0-and-compiling; (2) real variation operators (carried over, re-verified this session and worse than reported: 5 of the 6 mutation helpers — `inline_random_call`, `swap_equivalent`, `optimize_loop`, `add_parallel_hint`, `random_rewrite` — are literally empty functions, and the sixth routes through `random_subtree`, which returns a whole-tree clone; `mutate` is also GA-only, so it never runs at opt level 1 at all) — matters for diversity beyond the seed, less urgent now that the seed harvest dominates; (3) reconcile Z3 verification with executed behavior (carried over; the disagreement has changed shape — in all 3 runs exactly 4 winners are Z3-verified and all 4 measure tpr 1.000, but the other 8 tpr-1.000 winners per run are verified=false, so Z3 still certifies a different, narrower property than the tests measure). Suite after this branch: 116 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored.

> **Engine type-directed-fillings follow-up (2026-11-20, branch `feat/type-directed-fillings`):** blocker (1) above is FIXED. The hole's `expected_type` was recorded by seed construction but unreachable by the fillers — `HoleRef` carried only a path. `HoleRef` now captures `expected_type` where holes are found (`find_holes_rec`), and both filling entry points read it. `typed_literal_fillings(ty)` provides the literal menu per type (Bool → true/false; the integer family → 0/1; Float → 0.0; String → `""`; Char → `'a'`; Unit → `()`; List → empty list; Tuple composed recursively) and returns None for types with no honest literal menu — named/generic/function/Map/Set/Array, and Option (the IR has no Option literal node) — which keep the legacy menu untouched, as do all untyped holes (`expected_type: None`). For a typed hole, `generate_hole_fillings` returns the typed literals plus the spec tests' distinct expected outputs (return-typed by construction, admitted only through the conservative `node_matches_type` check, which recognizes only literal/collection shapes whose type is certain); `random_filling` draws from the typed menu only — no wrong-typed literal, no Return wrapper, no fresh Hole. Test-first: five new tests failed before the fix on exactly `Literal(Int(0))` evaluated for Bool/String/List holes and on a rollout-drawn unfilled Hole; a sixth guards that untyped holes keep the legacy menu. Probe (3 runs, same method): **winner tpr distribution unchanged — 36/42 at 1.000, 6/42 at the 0.500 no-tests neutral, 0/42 at 0.000; all 42 winners hole-free, all Mutation provenance. Compiles: 12/14 in every run (was 1/14)** — every tested spec now produces a compiling winner (wildcard arms read `_ => true`, `_ => "".to_string()` instead of `_ => 0`). Error classes across the 42 winner files collapse from 37× E0308 + 2× E0069 (Phase 9) to **9× E0308, 0× E0069, 0× E0425**. The only failing files are the two test-less specs (`tags_compatible`, `needs_parens`) in all 3 runs: with no tests there is no TestInduced seed and no truth signal, so their winners are still arbitrary random trees whose whole bodies are type-wrong at the top level (a `for` loop as the body of a Bool function; `vec![]` then `return op;` in a Bool function — the latter also trips a codegen statement-emission quirk, a missing `;` after the `vec![]` statement). Phase 9's 2× E0069 (a bare `return;` in a non-unit function) did not recur in 42 files: the Rust statement emitter always writes `return {expr};`, so those two were most likely random-tree winners whose `Return` wrapped an expression shape the expression emitter renders empty — that shape no longer wins anywhere, but with only two sightings ever, the class is dormant, not proven extinct. Next blockers, in order: (1) the test-less specs — nothing anywhere checks a candidate body's type against the spec's return type: generation is type-blind at the whole-body level, test-less scoring is the neutral 0.5, and selection cannot tell a Bool-bodied candidate from a loop-bodied one. A return-type check/filter for candidates (or tests for those two specs) is the remaining compile gap; it is a selection/generation discipline issue, not a filling issue. (2) Real variation operators (carried over, unchanged: 5 of the 6 mutation helpers are literally empty functions, the sixth routes through whole-tree-clone `random_subtree`, and `mutate` is GA-only so it never runs at opt level 1) — matters for diversity beyond the seed. (3) Reconcile Z3 verification with executed behavior (carried over, same shape: 12/42 winners are Z3-verified and all 12 measure tpr 1.000, but 24 of the 36 tpr-1.000 winners are verified=false, so Z3 still certifies a different, narrower property than the tests measure). Suite after this branch: 122 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored.

> **Engine return-type-gate follow-up (2026-11-20, branch `fix/candidate-return-type-gate`):** blocker (1) above is FIXED on the selection side — and the measurement shows precisely why selection alone cannot finish the job. `selector::return_type_verdict` is a conservative type inference over IR candidate bodies, mirroring the interpreter's evaluable subset: a type is claimed only when certain (literals; collections whose elements are certain and agree, with a wildcard for unprovable positions; BinOp/UnaryOp under certain operand rules; If/Match whose branches all agree; Let/Block tail expressions; Vars resolved against the spec's parameter types; known pure builtins — `len` → Int, the parser's `List` literal; Typed nodes), and anything else is Unknown, which is neutral. A provably mistyped `return` anywhere in the body is also a mismatch (rustc checks every return against the signature); integer-family types unify; a Generic in any position proves nothing. `select_best` applies a return-type gate immediately after the completeness gate, mirroring its shape: provably mistyped candidates are excluded while a provably matching or Unknown candidate exists, and if EVERY candidate is provably mistyped the gate falls back to ranking that pool unchanged (documented in the gate comment). Composite weights, tpr semantics and `evaluate_candidate` are untouched, and a regression test proves the tpr-1.0 seed-completion winner on a tested spec still wins with the gate active. The precise composed guarantee — whenever the hole-free pool contains a non-mistyped candidate, the winner is not mistyped — is locked in by a probe-pipeline integration test over both test-less specs; because the engine is randomized and the premise is not structural (measured premise rate ≈ 0.7 per synthesis attempt per spec), the test retries synthesis up to 8 times per spec and was verified stable over 30 consecutive runs. Probe (3 runs, same method, gate only): **winner tpr distribution unchanged — 36/42 at 1.000, 6/42 at the 0.500 no-tests neutral, 0/42 at 0.000; all 42 winners hole-free, all Mutation provenance; Z3-verified winners 12/42, all measuring tpr 1.000. Compiles: 12/14, 13/14, 12/14 (was 12/14 in every run). Error classes across the 42 files: 8× E0308, 0× E0069, 0× E0425 (was 9× E0308), plus 2 files failing on a codegen syntax slip (below).** The gate demonstrably works — provably mistyped bodies no longer win when a sound alternative exists — but compiles barely moved, for two measured reasons. (a) In roughly half of raw draws, a test-less spec's hole-free pool is UNIFORMLY mistyped (every MCTS completion inherits a certainly-wrong root shape — arithmetic roots, Int literals, Int `return`s), so the documented fallback crowns a mistyped winner anyway (2 of the 5 failing files in the final measurement are exactly this: bodies containing `return actual;` / `return parent_op;` in Bool functions). A selection gate cannot crown what the pool does not contain; the discipline gap is now in generation, not selection. (b) The most common surviving shape is a For-rooted body (`for i in 0..10 { … }` as a Bool function body): loops are Unknown by design — the interpreter cannot evaluate them either — so the gate is blind to them, while the emitted Rust gives a `for` tail type `()`, hence E0308. The codegen slip named in the previous note DID still appear in winner files after the gate (2 of 3 gate-only runs: `vec![]` with no `;` before `return` — a syntax error, "expected `;`, found keyword `return`"), so it was fixed as its own change: `ir_to_rust` emitted Collections in statement position tail-shaped; now the Collection arm terminates with `;`, and genuine value positions route through the existing tail renderer — `generate_rust` renders the function body via `ir_to_rust_tail` (the body's value IS the return value; statement-shaped bodies fall through byte-identically, so all previously compiling winners emit identical code, and bare-expression bodies — the `(actual + expected);` shape — now keep their value), and `ir_to_rust`'s If branches and Let bodies, the value positions of those constructs, route via `ir_to_rust_tail` with the return type as expectation, mirroring match arms. Re-measured after the codegen fix (3 fresh runs): **compiles 12/14, 12/14, 13/14; tpr distribution unchanged (36/42 at 1.000); error instances 6× E0308, 0× E0069, 0× E0425, and zero syntax/`;` errors — the slip class is gone** (a `vec![]` inside a loop body now correctly emits `vec![];`, removing the second E0308 those files used to carry). Remaining failures are the two test-less specs in 5 of 6 spec-runs, decomposed above: For-rooted Unknown winners (3 files) and uniformly-mistyped-pool fallback winners (2 files, one of which also exposed a pre-existing expression-emitter gap — an If condition the emitter cannot render comes out as `if /* UNSUPPORTED */`, a parse error unrelated to the `;` family). Next blockers, in order: (1) generation-side type discipline for test-less specs — the pool itself must contain sound hole-free candidates (type-directed root shapes / whole-body generation), since selection gates have nothing to crown in ~half of draws; alternatively give the two specs executable tests so they get a seed and a truth signal like the other twelve. (2) Codegen expression-emitter gaps (carried, newly evidenced): the `/* UNSUPPORTED */` condition emission, and the sibling statement arms that still emit unterminated tail shapes in statement position (`Call`/`Map`/`Filter`/`Fold`/`Sort`) — same latent hazard as the fixed Collection arm, not yet seen in winner files. (3) Real variation operators (carried over, unchanged: 5 of the 6 mutation helpers are literally empty functions, the sixth routes through whole-tree-clone `random_subtree`, and `mutate` is GA-only so it never runs at opt level 1). (4) Reconcile Z3 verification with executed behavior (carried over, same shape: 12/42 winners are Z3-verified and all 12 measure tpr 1.000, but 24 of the 36 tpr-1.000 winners are verified=false). Suite after this branch: 137 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored.
> **Engine type-directed-generation follow-up (2026-11-20, branch `feat/type-directed-generation`):** blocker (1) above is now FIXED on the generation side. `seed_random` — the only call site that creates fresh candidate bodies (grep-verified: GA mutation transforms existing bodies, MCTS fills holes in existing bodies) — now generates via `random_ir_tree_typed`, which threads the spec's declared return type through generation and reuses the verdict's own certainty rules (`selector::certainly_equal` / `int_family`, widened to `pub(crate)`; no second inference was written). The discipline: the root shape is generated in the return type's context (tail generator: plain typed expression, If/Match whose tails are generated in the same context, Let, Block ending in a typed tail, Return of a typed expression); a statement-only tree is never the entire body of a non-Unit function (loops appear only as statements inside a Block that ends in a typed tail, and statement generation never emits a Return); every Return wraps an expression generated for the return type (Returns come only from the tail generator, whose target is always the return type). Expression positions (operands, conditions, scrutinees, Let values, collection elements) use a separate expression generator, because the tail shapes are not renderable there. The shape menu is deliberately narrower than the verdict's typeable set — verdict-sound is not the same as renderable: no `Call` (codegen emits a call to a nonexistent free function, so the verdict's Int-typed `len(x)` would be E0425), no `Index`/`Head`/`Tail`/`Init` (unsupported in the expression emitter), no `Reverse` (emits `.reverse()`, which returns `()`), no `Concat` (emitted as `String + String`, which Rust rejects), no `Len` unary (emits `.len()` → usize vs the signature's i64); `Div`/`Mod` never take a constant-zero divisor (rustc's `unconditional_panic` lint rejects `x / 0`). For types with no literal menu (Named, Option, Map, …) the only leaf is an explicitly typed Hole — Unknown to the verdict, completable by the Phase 10 typed fillings. The legacy `random_ir_tree` / `random_ir_tree_scoped` are byte-for-byte unchanged for callers without a type context (regression-tested); the Phase 11 gate/verdict, composite weights, tpr semantics, the interpreter, Z3 and codegen are untouched. Measured baseline first (property test over the production seeding path, verdict-checked, 200 draws per M2 signature, written and run before the fix): seed bodies provably mistyped — is_known_type_tag 81/200, node_arity 27/200, type_tag_name 64/200, tags_compatible 69/200, needs_parens 73/200 — **314/1000 (31.4%) mistyped, only 13/1000 provably matching**. After the fix, the same test measures **0/1000 mistyped and 1000/1000 provably matching** (two runs): every shape the typed generator emits for these signatures is certainly typed under the verdict's rules, and typed generation emits no Holes for menufull types — so the sound-pool premise is now structural rather than sampled. Premise rate for the two test-less specs (fraction of synthesis attempts whose returned pool contains a hole-free non-mistyped candidate; ≈0.53–0.7 per attempt in the Phase 11 measurement): **30/30 attempts per spec in two independent batches (60/60)**. Probe (3 runs, same method): **winner tpr distribution unchanged — 36/42 at 1.000, 6/42 at the 0.500 no-tests neutral, 0/42 at 0.000; all 42 winners hole-free, all Mutation provenance; Z3-verified winners 12/42, all measuring tpr 1.000. Compiles: 14/14, 14/14, 14/14 (was 12/14, 12/14, 13/14). Error instances across the 42 winner files: 0× E0308 (was 6×), 0 syntax errors, 0× E0069, 0× E0425 — the first probe measurement with no failing winner file at all.** The two test-less winners are now typed-generation shapes (e.g. `return ((true || false) && (!false));` for tags_compatible; a Let + If/Match over the Int params with Bool arms for needs_parens): type-sound and compiling, but still semantically arbitrary — with no executable tests there is no truth signal for these two specs, and there cannot be one until the spec syntax can bind tuple test inputs, which is a language-design decision and deliberately not made here. Next blockers, in order: (1) Codegen expression-emitter gaps (carried): an unrenderable shape in expression position emits `/* UNSUPPORTED */` (seen in a Phase 11 fallback winner's If condition), and the `Call`/`Map`/`Filter`/`Fold`/`Sort` statement arms still emit unterminated tail shapes in statement position — the typed generator avoids these shapes in fresh bodies, but MCTS completions and GA mutations can still produce them. (2) Real variation operators (carried over, unchanged: 5 of the 6 mutation helpers are literally empty functions, the sixth routes through whole-tree-clone `random_subtree`, and `mutate` is GA-only so it never runs at opt level 1). (3) Reconcile Z3 verification with executed behavior (carried over, same shape: 12/42 winners are Z3-verified and all 12 measure tpr 1.000, but 24 of the 36 tpr-1.000 winners are verified=false). Suite after this branch: 139 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored.
